# Druid Class quest - Legendary Adept, Archdruid

## Post 77121 by Tenyar — 2023-11-13T03:55:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=77121#p77121 | page 1 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

This quest chain is envisioned to be part of the "Legendary Adept Hero class" system, found [HERE](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=11617).

One of my favorite quest chains in WoW is the Warlock's Dreadsteed mount, hands down.  This quest chain, and hopefully the ones for all the other classes, will aim to recapture that feeling.
![Image](https://wallpapers.com/images/hd/world-of-warcraft-restoration-druid-healing-69ucodb01a3oyfab.jpg)
This quest chain will have players embark on a journey to attain the revered status of an Archdruid. The quest begins with a personal invitation from Malfurion Stormrage, who recognizes the player's deep connection with nature and their potential to ascend further. The journey involves a series of challenging and symbolic trials, each focusing on different aspects of the Druid's connection with nature - from harnessing the energies of sacred Moonwells across Azeroth to embodying the essence of various animal forms.

Players must demonstrate mastery over the Druidic arts, including challenges requiring specific use of their animal forms, and a deep understanding of nature's balance. The trials take the player to various significant locations within Azeroth, such as Felwood, Feralas, and the Alterac Mountains, each offering unique challenges and experiences.

Upon successful completion of these trials, the player receives powerful items that not only serve as a testament to their achievements but also significantly enhance their abilities. The final step of the journey is a return to Malfurion Stormrage, where the player is officially recognized as an Archdruid, marking their place among the elite protectors of nature in Azeroth. This journey is not just about gaining power but also about understanding and embodying the deep wisdom and responsibility that comes with the title of Archdruid.
 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Upon reaching level 60, the druid will receive a letter in their Mailbox From: Malfurion Stormrage

Subject: A Summoning from the Archdruid

Greetings, [Player Name],

In your journey across Azeroth, you have shown a dedication and mastery of the druidic arts that few have achieved. Your connection to nature, to the ebb and flow of life and Azeroth's ancient spirits, has not gone unnoticed.

I find myself eager to speak with you, to share knowledge and perhaps guide you onto a path few druids have tread - the ascension to Archdruid.

When you feel the time is right, make your journey to Moonglade. I await our conversation amidst the sacred groves.

Walk with the grace of Elune,

Malfurion Stormrage

Which will give them the quest: [A Summoning from the Archdruid](https://tinyurl.com/A-Summoning).

Should they decide to meet with Malfurion, he will give them the quest: [Echoes of Archdruidry](https://tinyurl.com/Echoes-of-Archdruidry) Which will have them listen to some history of Archdruids.
Long ago, when Azeroth was still young and the continents unscarred by war, the land was teeming with untamed magic. The natural energies of the world flowed without direction, giving life to the magnificent, the perilous, and the arcane. The creatures and beings of old roamed freely, each following their primal instincts.

Among them were the earliest of our kind, the Druids, who felt a unique connection to Azeroth's spirit. They communed with the land, learned its secrets, and yearned to harmonize with its rhythms. Yet with great power came great challenges. The untamed magics sometimes lashed out, causing imbalance and chaos.

From this urgency rose the first Archdruids. These were druids whose bond with nature was unparalleled, whose wisdom was sought by both beast and mortal. The Archdruids did not merely wield the energies of the land; they became its stewards. They traveled across Azeroth, soothing the raging magics, calming the restless spirits, and ensuring that life and magic coexisted in harmony.

Time passed, and the challenges facing Azeroth evolved. But the role of the Archdruids remained unchanged: they were Azeroth's guardians, ensuring that the balance between nature and civilization was maintained. They built sanctuaries, groves where the wounded land could heal, where animals could find refuge, and where druids could train and learn.

An Archdruid's role is not merely that of a guardian. They are the harmonizers of the natural world, ensuring that life and magic ebb and flow in equilibrium. When the Emerald Nightmare sought to corrupt the Dream, it was the Archdruids who stood at the forefront, pushing back the encroaching darkness. When the World Trees needed guidance and protection, the Archdruids were there, singing songs of growth and rejuvenation.

But being an Archdruid is also a path of sacrifice. They give of themselves, often becoming one with the land, trees, or waters, ensuring that Azeroth remains a haven for all life. Their spirits often linger, watching over sacred groves and ancient forests, ensuring that the balance they fought so hard to maintain endures.

Young druid, as you stand here, know that you too carry the potential to join this ancient order. Your connection with nature, your deeds, and your heart all show promise. But the path to becoming an Archdruid is fraught with trials. It is a journey of self-discovery, of understanding the deepest secrets of Azeroth, and of making sacrifices for the greater good.

Your journey has showcased a bond to nature reminiscent of the first Archdruids. The path ahead will not be easy. It will challenge your spirit, your resolve, and your very essence. But remember, just as the ancient Archdruids shaped Azeroth's destiny, so too can you. The potential within you is vast, waiting to be realized, waiting to echo in the annals of history, as one of Azeroth's revered Archdruids.

In the echoes of the ancient forests, in the murmur of the running streams, and in the rustling of the leaves, Azeroth calls out for its guardians. The question is, are you ready to answer that call?

After finishing his story, he will offer the Druid the quest: [Path of the Feral](https://tinyurl.com/Path-of-the-Feral).

This will send the Druid to Felwood to meet Eridan Bluewind and start the first Trial. Eridan will offer the Druid the quest: [Trial of the Claw](https://tinyurl.com/Trial-of-the-Claw). This trial takes place at a nearby ruin, and is two phases.

Phase One: Phase one of this trial summons several waves of ghost bears that drain HP, have very high armor and resistance, but will run away and disappear whenever you use the growl ability in your Bear Form.

and Phase Two: Phase Two, the waves keep coming, the Druid's HP drops to approx, 25%, but they get a buff that increases auto attack speed, damage and armor massively.

The idea here is the Druid is connecting with the Bear spirit, first the Druid can't damage the spirits, so they get defensive; Growl and scare them away. That doesn't work, so they switch, and have to go damage mode and fight like..well..a Bear.

Completing this trial Eridan gives the Druid: [Guided by the Tides](https://tinyurl.com/Guided-by-the-Tides)

After traveling to Azshara and finding Keeper Murglnc, he wil give the Druid: [Trial of the Endless Depths](https://tinyurl.com/Trial-of-the-Endless-Depths)

This trial will require to use their Aquatic Form and search the waters of Azshara to find the Abyssal Makrura, defeat it, and retrieve the [Luminescent Pearl](https://dev.turtlecraft.gg/?fbclid=IwAR3zn7hHUc3PkltN-72vEfatyU7E7HLY6r8lKDN9bw1AL3lTnzwMTghgFro#!).

After handing in the Pearl to Murglnc, he will direct the Druid to Hillsbrad Foothills with the quest: [Echoes of the Tides](https://tinyurl.com/Echoes-of-the-Tides).

After finding Moren Riverbend in Hillsbrad Foothills, he will task the druid with the quest: [Trial of the Silent Prowler](https://dev.turtlecraft.gg/#!~). Which will require the Druid to venture up into the Alterac Mountains and obtain a [Sentinel's Feather](https://dev.turtlecraft.gg/?fbclid=IwAR3lMwXs_wxGY5ip7U89j0zhiCQ6nNeyiPLtYk0QZNE5U1jFxJe0LuQjOMg#!). Functionally it'll work the same as a Rogues pickpocket; thematically the Druid is mastering the grace and agility of the Cat. They've gotten so good they can pluck a birds feathers without it noticing.

Turning the feather back in will sent the Druid back to Malfurion via: [Returning to Roots](https://tinyurl.com/Returning-to-Roots).

Malfurion will have the Druid wake up 4 Ancient Protectors and get their Wisdom. With the quest: [Awakening the Ancients](https://tinyurl.com/Awakening-the-Ancients).

This quest will send the Druid to various places to wake Slumbering Ancients. Before getting their Wisdom, the Druid must answer a riddle from each. Each is a challenging test of the Druid's wisdom. Solving this riddle requires a deeper contemplation of nature's subtleties.

Riddle One: With moon's soft glow and sun's warm kiss,
I transform and adapt, both hiss and bliss.
In nature's embrace, I find my groove,
With every form, I seamlessly move.
Who am I?

A chameleon in the jungle.
The tide of the Great Sea.
The cycle of the seasons.
A Druid of Azeroth. Answer: A Druid of Azeroth.

Riddle Two: In forest deep and mountain tall, I thrive in life, yet embrace the fall. A friend to man and beast I be, yet chained to neither land nor sea. What am I?

A River
The Wind
A Tree
A Fish Answer: The Wind.

Riddle Three: I dance with flame but drown in frost, breathe with the earth, yet am never lost. Born of chaos, stilled in peace, a force untamed that never shall cease. What am I?

A Mountain
A Storm
A Bird
A River Answer: A Storm

Riddle Four: I am the whisper in the night, the unseen growth that takes no light. In cycles of the moon, I wax and wane, in forest's heart, I leave my stain. What am I?

The Wind
The Moon
A Shadow
A Mushroom Answer: A Mushroom

Answering each riddle correctly will give the Druid the Respective Ancients Wisdom, as well as an Ancient Blossom.
[Ancient Blossom](https://dev.turtlecraft.gg/?fbclid=IwAR3TUUWMbP1vV17AM3HkWV-3BXChGaaf6f3M3qqd6-1KBrRql-lUmiJexCQ#!)
[Warden of Un'Goro's wisdom](https://dev.turtlecraft.gg/?fbclid=IwAR0L-Soq3fZi16nqlln5fgmLEc_iLpbBdPS86imJRQTx5WYAHkYwGvMdQag#!)
[Sentinel of Winterspring's wisdom](https://dev.turtlecraft.gg/?fbclid=IwAR0txmaaRKwTT_zzIO3N1uEqzGCUT4wQZhFdq3GYo276mPnXKrKLgNFId0M#!)
[Guardian of Felwood's wisdom](https://dev.turtlecraft.gg/?fbclid=IwAR0UPzis05zSHL_Icfeae8sHjWy3AuLeWjld36agBDUyJCuQKcLHL0d1iRY#!)
[Protector of Ashenvale's Wisdom](https://dev.turtlecraft.gg/?fbclid=IwAR3LCDT-3E2tCMvhGzlRROWqkjfU50E8YfdjXkqNCkEo_lEojdLhQIU1iCQ#!)

Returning to Malfurion with the Ancient's Wisdom, the Druid is tasked with taking [Malfurions Lunar Amulet](https://tinyurl.com/Malfurions-Lunar-Amulet) to various Moonwells around Azeroth to charge it with their power with the quest: [The Amulet of Lunar Resurgence](https://tinyurl.com/The-Amulet-of-Lunar-Resurgence)

Returning to Malfurion with the charged Amulet he gives the Druid the Penultimate quest in the chain; As they will use everything they've gathered so far in [Rebirth of the Emerald Dream](https://tinyurl.com/Rebirth-of-the-Emerald-Dream)

Malfurion sends the Druid into the new Emerald Sanctum raid to use the Amulet to cleanse corruption, use the scrolls of wisdom to weaken and kill one of the bosses in the raid, and finally plant all four Ancient Blossoms to help regrow the Emerald Dream.

Completing all this and returning to Malfurion will wrap everything up, with  [The Ascension to Archdruid](https://tinyurl.com/Ascension-to-Archdruid)

It'll spawn Cenarius, Hamuul Runetotem, as well as some other important Druid people. Some other citizens from around Moonglade be around there.

Finishing this will give the Druid the title of Archdruid, as well as replace some of their current spells with "upgraded" versions of themselves, and several new spells. seen below. Also for offer will be a choice between a few items worthy of an Archdruid.

## Post 77150 by Mativh (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2023-11-13T08:14:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=77150#p77150 | page 1 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

The concept of further character development after max level is a good one, I also like the idea of alternative version of abilities being available after completing certain challenges, but there a few issues here:

Archdruids:

Archdruid is the highest rank a druid can hold, awarded only by the Cenarion Circle. There are only a few archdruids on Azeroth, most of which directly studied under Cenarius himself. An archdruid is an immensely wise and powerful druid whose influence on nature **surpasses that of lower-ranking druids**.

First of all, lore-wise to become an Archdruid especially after the death of Cenarius, is an extremely exclusive title among Druids, much more than the challenges you have proposed, it's not something that should be given away as a participation trophy. Even if the challenges were made more difficult and required expensive consumables and some skill, most max levels would go around being ArchDruids..
Archdruid should really be someone who has fully mastered their class; reached level 60 in hardcore + got high ranking in PvP and defeated most raid bosses, on top of custom challenges.
In Legion all Druids only had to do a quest on level 45 to get the Archdruid title...
If everyone is an Archdruid, noone is.
I don't think that is your intention, but the way this concept is formulated, it is very much like the Champion/saver of the world design in retail wow, that went to an extreme in Legion where everyone was going around with a Scythe of Elune/ Ashbringer etc.
This is a power fantasy of modern single player rpgs, even there it takes from the game, let alone in an mmorpg.

Next is the "nature" part. The druidism in Warcraft has been split in the Night Elven society to Elune worship for Priestesses and the Sentinels, and nature-based for Druids. In WoW the Night Elf Priest is a generic standardized class, that can either be a human-holy-light priest or a forsaken-shadow-ascendant priest. And the Elune related things were thrown at the priest as a few racials as well as given to Balance Druids which is going against the lore.
In retail, progressively the nature part has been diminishing from the Druid class, the lunar theme got extended by solar and astral even further, which is absolutely lore-breaking.
The Priestesses of Elune should be mainly about lunar/nocturnal/astral themes, with a touch of Druidism (like the owl scout).
Druids should be all about nature / emerald dream, only with a touch of astronomy.
It is enough that instead of nature oriented abilities, the Cenarius Circle Druids that emerged from the Emerald dream are now casting Elune-oriented spells, if on top of it you'd make those spells that are nature-based, also turned into Elune-based as an "elite" version at max level.

You cant just add celestial to an ability that is channeling an entirely different force (and the channleing of that force requires an entirely different approach) in the warcraft universe, and then have the target be susceptible to the initial force. It's as if you made "Divine pyroblast", changing the pyroblast to holy damage plus adding susceptibility to fire. Altough lore-wise pyroblast is a fiery expression of arcane magic, it is an entirely different force from fel-based fire but the game uses the same school of magic for both.. still in pyroblasts case you could pull off fire-arcane interaction. You need to have a throughout understanding of the lore, not only events, the races history but also worldbuilding, cosmology, philosophy, like the devs did that put it together in the first place. In order to make spells that make sense, as well as changes in the society of races, and their classes. In retail, the franchise was bought by a different company at one point, and most original developers left, the new ones have no insight into the warcrafts world, and keep adding things with superficial relation.

And especially for Tauren Druids that don't even have Elune/nocturnal themes as part of their society, that would make no sense at all, retail developers get lost in abstractions and make the game not be grounded and the worlds coherence and immersion are destroyed by it, which ties to the;

Lastly, I've seen the generic suggestion of this, and I know you want to deepen the class fantasy, but it shouldnt be approached like the class halls of the legion expansion, it would further standardize the classes. These challenges could be intetesting if they took into account the games lore, not only the lore of the WoW classes that are an amalgamation of the warcraft lore bits for the sake of MMO balancing.

Overall, I think you have woven into your perspective too much the retail mindset. Play more Turtle WoW and then you'll see what I mean. But the concept you are proposing has potential and in a way it is in line with the Turtle WoW mentality; which is a focus on the journey rather than destination, and the max level character progression could be turned into more of a journey. Some spells get for example max ranks in AQ, but there could also be other things, like new abilities and alternative versions of them depending on what way the player choses to go after max level.. but it needs to be approached with the vanilla mindset.

## Post 77156 by Shambakriger — 2023-11-13T10:02:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=77156#p77156 | page 1 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

+1 for immersive class quests
challenging mixed solo/group content like the benediction, rok'delar or dreadsteed chain has always been a hit. Even the mage tower from legion is a great example. Your quest chain seems very grounded and fleshed out.
That being said, I fully agree with Mativh that the title of Archdruid should not be attainable by players. Druids are already the strongest class lorewise ingame, matching the exclusivity of later hero classes like death knight and demon hunter.
There only exists a handful of archdruids in the world, so giving the title to players would give us a "main character" experience like in retail, which is not what vanilla is about.
It's also problematic tying so many spell upgrades to a single quest chain, as this would make the quest chain the first mandatory thing to do once you hit 60. Instead I think you should lower the scope, both for the sake of balance and for lore, and just have a simple reward in the form of a strong item or cosmetic reward.
